observations.text: SP performed the close trail exercise at the level desired for this Training Section, taking the No2 position behind the leader only after the IP directed the initial closure and part of the stabilization. Nose-tail separation was then held at the 3 to 4 ship length values and the A/C was kept below the leader's exhaust throughout the turns. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent establishment of the close trail position without the IP's direction is expected to improve.

SP, following the IP's verbal indications on power and closure, established and maintained the close trail position as No2 through the turns and the modified Lazy "8". Nose-tail separation was held at the 3 to 4 ship length values and vertical separation at the 15 feet below the leader's exhaust value, with the A/C never allowed above the exhaust line. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, but no intervention on the controls was required from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP established the close trail position on own initiative and flew the modified Chandelle behind the leader without the IP's intervention. Nose-tail separation opened past 2 and up to nearly 3 ship lengths, between the 2 and 3 ship length values, and vertical separation reached some 9 feet below the leader's exhaust, between the 5 and 15 feet values. Both minor deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained the close trail position as No2 with accuracy and speed through the turns, the modified Lazy "8" and the modified Barrel Rolls. Nose-tail separation was held within the 1 to 2 ship length values, never less than 1 ship length and never further than 2, and the A/C was kept between 0 and 5 feet below the leader's exhaust. No verbal indication was required from the IP at any point of the sequence. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated the leader's energy changes and held the close trail position with exceptional accuracy in power and pitch control. Nose-tail separation was kept near the middle of the 1 to 2 ship length band with negligible deviation, and vertical separation stayed within 2 feet of the leader's exhaust line and never above it. The position was regained instantly after each unload, without abrupt inputs and with positive Gs maintained at all times. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a late and insufficient power reduction as the leader unloaded at the top of the modified Lazy "8", did not maintain the close trail position of 1 to 2 ship lengths of nose-tail separation and closed inside 1 ship length. The IP took the controls and repositioned the A/C aft and below the leader's exhaust. The close trail position could not be re-established without assistance. Further study of the close trail closure and power technique of the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation behind the leader, did not keep the A/C slightly below the leader's exhaust and allowed the No2 position to rise above the exhaust line during the modified Barrel Roll. Nose-tail separation opened at the same time beyond 4 ship lengths, outside the 3 to 4 ship length values. The IP directed the recovery, executed part of the reposition and terminated the maneuver. The exercise was not completed without assistance.

SP maintained the close trail position within the standards desired for this Training Section, holding nose-tail separation at the 3 to 4 ship length values and vertical separation at 15 feet below the leader's exhaust. Corrections in the turns were initiated only after the IP's verbal indications, and the tendency was to fall aft rather than to anticipate the leader's power changes. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier and independent recognition of the developing nose-tail separation is expected to improve.

SP, as leader, smoothly carried out the turns and the modified Chandelle with No2 in close trail, maintaining positive Gs and orientation within the assigned flight area. Airspeed at the recovery briefly reached the 250 KIAS upper end of the 120 to 250 KIAS range and bank in one turn slightly exceeded the briefed value while remaining under the 90 degree maximum. SP recognized both minor deviations and corrected them in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained the close trail position with accuracy and speed, holding nose-tail separation within the 1 to 2 ship length values and never flying less than 1 ship length or further than 2. Vertical separation was kept between 0 and 5 feet below the leader's exhaust throughout the turns and the modified Lazy "8", with no verbal indications required from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP read the leader's energy state early and held the close trail position with exceptional accuracy in power, pitch and G control. Deviations from the 1 to 2 ship length nose-tail separation and from the 0 to 5 feet below the leader's exhaust were negligible through the turns, the modified Chandelle and the modified Barrel Rolls. The position was regained immediately after every energy change, without any abrupt input and with the A/C never above the exhaust line. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect stick and power technique in the pull-down of the modified Lazy "8", did not maintain positive Gs as No2 and allowed the A/C to drift above the leader's exhaust with nose-tail separation opening beyond 4 ship lengths. The IP intervened on the controls to reposition the A/C behind and below the leader. The close trail position was not maintained without assistance. Further study of the close trail references and of the smooth control technique for the precision maneuvers is required.

SP, as leader, due to failure to make the knock-it-off call when the briefed parameters were exceeded, did not smoothly carry out the modified Barrel Roll with No2 in close trail and allowed bank to pass 90 degrees with airspeed decaying below the 120 KIAS lower end of the range. The IP called the knock-it-off, took the controls and separated the formation. The maneuver could not be completed without the IP's assistance. Further study of the entry parameters and energy management for the precision maneuvers is required.

SP, as leader, due to an abrupt and uneven pull into the modified Chandelle, did not smoothly carry out the maneuver with No2 in close trail and reached the 3 G and 90 degree bank limits of the briefed envelope. Airspeed at the top decayed to the 120 KIAS lower end of the range before the profile was re-established. The parameters were corrected only after the IP's verbal indications, with delayed recognition of the developing deviation.

SP, due to an inadequate anti-G straining manoeuvre for the G applied in the 3 G portion of the modified Chandelle, did not hold the nose-tail reference on the leader and fell aft to the 3 to 4 ship length values while sinking to 15 feet below the leader's exhaust. The correction on power and pitch was initiated only after the IP's verbal cue. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP maintained the close trail position within the standards desired for this Training Section, holding nose-tail separation between the 2 and 3 ship length values and vertical separation some 8 feet below the leader's exhaust. The small deviations in the turns were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, although the position was consistently aft of the briefed 1 to 2 ship lengths. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a closer and more stable nose-tail separation is expected to improve.

SP, as leader, smoothly carried out the turns, the modified Lazy "8" and the modified Chandelle with No2 held in close trail, maintaining positive Gs at all times and orientation within the assigned flight area. Airspeed was kept well inside the 120 to 250 KIAS range, bank within the 90 degree maximum and loading within 3 Gs, with accurate and prompt corrections and no intervention from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated the leader's power and G changes and flew the close trail position with exceptional precision through the modified Barrel Rolls. Deviations from the 1 to 2 ship length nose-tail separation and from the 0 to 5 feet below the leader's exhaust were negligible, the A/C being held near the middle of the band and within 2 feet of the exhaust line. Positive Gs were maintained at all times and no correction was required at any point of the sequence. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to over-controlling in pitch while chasing the leader's exhaust in the modified Barrel Roll, did not maintain the close trail position and allowed nose-tail separation to open past 4 ship lengths with the A/C above the leader's exhaust line. The IP took the controls and repositioned the A/C behind and below the leader. Close trail could not be maintained without the IP's assistance. Further study of the close trail references and of the smooth control technique of the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP, due to a false attitude perception that was not resolved against the instruments while fixated on the leader's exhaust, did not hold the close trail position through the modified Lazy "8" and did not maintain orientation within the assigned flight area. Nose-tail separation exceeded 4 ship lengths and the A/C climbed above the leader's exhaust line. The IP directed the knock-it-off and executed the separation and the return to the assigned area. The exercise was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to a late and excessive power reduction each time the leader unloaded, did not maintain the close trail position of 1 to 2 ship lengths of nose-tail separation and stabilized at the 3 to 4 ship length values through the turns and the modified Chandelle. Vertical separation was allowed to reach 15 feet below the leader's exhaust. The position was closed up only after the IP's verbal indications, with delayed recognition of the developing deviation.

SP, due to acceptance of a previously uncorrected deviation as the new working standard, flew the close trail position at the 3 to 4 ship length values instead of the required 1 to 2 ship lengths of nose-tail separation, and settled 15 feet below the leader's exhaust. SP did not identify the spacing as out of standard until the IP's verbal indications, after which the position was closed up and held. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to a slightly late pitch correction at the leader's roll-in, did not hold nose-tail separation within the 1 to 2 ship length values and opened past 2 and up to nearly 3 ship lengths, between the 2 and 3 ship length values, in two of the turns. Vertical separation momentarily reached some 8 feet below the leader's exhaust, between the 5 and 15 feet values. Both minor deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn, did not keep the A/C slightly below the leader's exhaust during the modified Lazy "8" and sank to some 10 feet below it, between the 5 and 15 feet values. Nose-tail separation opened at the same time past 2 and up to nearly 3 ship lengths, between the 2 and 3 ship length values. SP recognized both minor deviations and corrected them in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention.

SP maintained the close trail position as No2 with accuracy and speed, holding nose-tail separation within the 1 to 2 ship length values and the A/C between 0 and 5 feet below the leader's exhaust. The position was however held at the 2 ship length limit through most of the modified Lazy "8" and the modified Barrel Rolls, with the margin to the further-than-2 limit consumed at each unload. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more stable nose-tail separation nearer the middle of the 1 to 2 ship length band is expected to improve.

SP anticipated every energy change of the leader and flew the close trail position with exceptional precision through the turns, the modified Lazy "8", the modified Chandelle and the modified Barrel Rolls. Deviations from the 1 to 2 ship length nose-tail separation and from the 0 to 5 feet below the leader's exhaust were negligible, the A/C being held near the middle of the band and within 2 feet of the exhaust line. Positive Gs were maintained throughout and no correction was required from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.
